results.question: Is Zenovax volume growing or declining month over month?
results.reason: plan matches and the request succeeded
results.sql:
WITH pac_periods AS (
  SELECT c.period_mo AS label, min(c.wk_offset) AS newest, count(*) AS weeks,
         min(CASE WHEN %s = ANY(c.sources) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AS covered
  FROM app_ref.calendar c
  GROUP BY c.period_mo), pac_numbered AS (
  SELECT label, covered, weeks,
         row_number() OVER (ORDER BY newest DESC) AS pos
  FROM pac_periods), pac_requested AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.period_mo AS label FROM app_ref.calendar c
  WHERE c.mo_offset = ANY(%s)), pac_span AS (
  SELECT min(n.pos) - %s AS lo, max(n.pos) AS hi
  FROM pac_numbered n JOIN pac_requested r ON r.label = n.label), pac_spine AS (
  SELECT n.label, n.covered, n.weeks, n.pos,
         n.label IN (SELECT label FROM pac_requested) AS requested
  FROM pac_numbered n CROSS JOIN pac_span sp
  WHERE n.pos BETWEEN sp.lo AND sp.hi), pac_series AS (
SELECT s.period_mo AS dim0_id, s.period_mo AS dim0_label, SUM(s.pack_units) AS value
FROM sales s
JOIN products p ON p.ndc = s.ndc
WHERE s.data_source = ANY(%s) AND s.brand_flag = 1 AND s.period_mo IN (SELECT label FROM pac_spine) AND upper(p.drug_name) = ANY(%s)
GROUP BY s.period_mo, s.period_mo
), pac_dense AS (
  SELECT sp.label AS dim0_id, sp.label AS dim0_label, sp.pos, sp.requested, sp.weeks,
         CASE WHEN sp.covered THEN COALESCE(se.value, 0) END AS value
  FROM pac_spine sp
  LEFT JOIN pac_series se ON se.dim0_id = sp.label), pac_lagged AS (
  SELECT dim0_id, dim0_label, requested, value, weeks,
         lag(value) OVER (ORDER BY pos) AS prior_value,
         lag(weeks) OVER (ORDER BY pos) AS prior_weeks
  FROM pac_dense)
SELECT dim0_id, dim0_label, prior_value,
       value - prior_value AS change,
       CASE WHEN prior_value > 0
            THEN (value - prior_value)::numeric / prior_value END AS change_pct,
       weeks, prior_weeks, value
FROM pac_lagged WHERE requested
ORDER BY dim0_id ASC
LIMIT 5001

answer.period_note: Reporting window: r3m — the rolling 3 months (current month plus the two prior).

A period with no purchases is shown as zero. A period a data source did not cover is left blank, not zero.

Each month is compared with the month before it, including the month just before the window. The change is blank for the first month of the data, and wherever either month is unknown. The percentage is blank where the earlier month was zero or negative; the change in packs is still shown.

A reporting month holds the weeks that end in it, so months differ in length (4 or 5 weeks for a month); a total moves with its number of weeks even when the weekly rate does not. Each row shows both months' week counts.

results.question: Compare our market share across all market categories
results.sql:
WITH num AS (
SELECT SUM(s.pack_units * p.unit_conversion_factor) AS value
FROM sales s
JOIN products p ON p.ndc = s.ndc
WHERE s.data_source = ANY(%s) AND s.brand_flag = 1 AND s.mo_offset = ANY(%s)
), den AS (
SELECT SUM(s.pack_units * p.unit_conversion_factor) AS value
FROM sales s
JOIN products p ON p.ndc = s.ndc
WHERE s.data_source = ANY(%s) AND s.mo_offset = ANY(%s) AND p.market_subcategory IN (SELECT DISTINCT market_subcategory FROM products WHERE brand_flag = 1)
)
SELECT n.value AS numerator, d.value AS denominator,
       n.value / NULLIF(d.value, 0) AS value
FROM num n CROSS JOIN den d

answer.headline: Market share is 146.00% (328,723.10 equivalents against a reported market of 225,147.08 equivalents).
answer.period_note: Reporting window: r3m — the rolling 3 months (current month plus the two prior).
notes: This window includes the current reporting period, which is still accumulating.
warnings: Market share here divides our distributor volume by the reported market total. In this dataset the market source contains only competitor products, so the denominator understates the true total market. Treat these percentages as indicative of relative position, not as a reliable share.
This value exceeds 100%, which is not a real market share. It means the reported market volume is smaller than our own shipments, so the sources are inconsistent rather than the share being genuine.
